title: Availability query distinguishes maintenance period from manual restriction
gherkin:
Feature: Availability State Semantics Separation
  Scenario: Distinguish maintenance period from manual restriction
    Given an item with a scheduled maintenance period from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-20
    And the same item has a manual restriction applied
    When I query the availability status for the item
    Then the response must indicate the maintenance period as a distinct unavailability reason
    And the response must indicate the manual restriction as a separate unavailability reason
    And the two reasons must not be conflated in the same status field
rationale: Maintenance periods block rental activity but require distinct representation from manual restrictions. Users need to understand whether an item is unavailable due to scheduled maintenance (temporary, predictable) versus manual restrictions (administrative decision). This directly addresses the operative requirement that availability state semantics must separate maintenance periods from manual restrictions.
usedContextItems: Availability state semantics must separate maintenance periods from manual restrictions and from item lifecycle terminal states|Availability query results must clearly indicate the reason or category of unavailability to prevent user confusion about item recoverability|Maintenance periods block rental activity and render items non-rentable, but may require distinct UI/API representation from other unavailability reasons
